metadata.title: SHIELD-AI to NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (DRAFT, MS, IAM, DS, TP, MIR, GRM and EE pillars)
metadata.remarks: AI-assisted draft. Not reviewed by a control SME. See crosswalk/REPORT.md for fit and residuals.

provenance.mapping-description: Functional mapping (NIST IR 8477) from SHIELD-AI controls to SP 800-53 Rev 5.2.0. Scope: MS, IAM, DS, TP, MIR, GRM and EE pillars (69 of 69 controls). One map entry per control pair so each relationship and confidence is individually reviewable. Targets are base controls or enhancements, mapped at control level, not statement level.

maps.remarks: Separate execution domain per process is the generic form of one sandbox per agent.
Boundary mechanisms isolating supporting components; sandbox boundary is one such mechanism.
Fail in a known state covers the 'fail-closed on isolation breach' clause only.
Baseline configuration is the nearest home for the immutable-infrastructure clause; it does not require immutability.
Enforcing approved authorizations for access to infrastructure APIs.
No implicit access beyond what the registered tool requires is least privilege.
Deny-by-default is network-level in 800-53; EE-02 is API-level. Related, not equivalent.
Allocating resources by quota is the core requirement.
Resource exhaustion/DoS; SC-5 is oriented to external DoS events, EE-03 also covers a compromised agent as the source.
Alerting when limits are exceeded is a monitoring function.
Analyse changes in a separate test environment before production.
Protect preproduction environments commensurate with risk.
Logical access restrictions on changes to the system.
Integrity verification tools (the filesystem integrity monitoring clause).
Allow-by-exception for what may execute; adjacent to the write-path allowlist.
Fail in a known state; EE-06 specifies the state (halted, alerting).
Verify correct operation of security functions and alert on failure.
Fail-safe procedures when failures occur.
Enforce access restrictions associated with changes to the system.
Authorize access to security functions; the agent must not hold it for its own controls.
Configuration change control and approval.
Documented, approved configuration settings and deviations.
Separate test environments.
Protecting preproduction environments.
Verifying a control is operating, here by active test, is related to function verification.
Identifiers may be assigned to an individual, group, role, service or device; uniqueness is required.
Identity providers managing non-person entity (NPE) identities: the closest 800-53 term for agents.
Uniquely identify and authenticate services before communications.
Audit records carry the identity of the subject, which is how actions are attributed to an agent.
Associates the user's identification with processes acting for them. See qualifier.

qualifiers.subject: both
qualifiers.description: IA-2 binds a process to the identity of the user it acts for; IAM-01 requires an agent identity distinct from the human's. These are compatible if the agent has its own identity and a delegation link to the user, but an implementer who satisfies IA-2 by letting agents run under the user's identity would fail IAM-01.

maps.remarks: Least privilege for processes acting on behalf of users.
Enforcing approved authorizations, including no self-escalation.
Attribute-based policy is one way to express per-agent tool/data scope.
Human reviews under defined conditions; scoped to information flows, not arbitrary actions.
Separation of duties covers the 'agent cannot approve its own action' clause.
Protecting authenticators; covers the gateway/operator token clause.
Dual authorization; a human approval gate is similar in shape but not in definition.
Authenticator management: storage, protection, change.
Protection of authenticators commensurate with the access they grant.
Automatically remove or disable temporary accounts after a defined period.
Authenticator lifetime and refresh.
Prohibits use of cached authenticators after a period; related to stale-credential replay.
Prevent unintended information transfer via shared system resources.
Separation of information flows by type.
No session may exercise access authorised to another.
Accountability and traceability design principle: trace security-relevant actions to the entity on whose behalf they are taken; covers the chain-reconstruction clause.
Audit records identifying subjects; covers only the chain-reconstruction fragment.
Non-repudiation of actions performed by a process on behalf of an individual.
Limiting what a delegated principal can do; does not address depth.
Least privilege applied to credential scope.
Authenticator lifecycle.
Revocation of access authorizations when attributes change.
Enforce authorizations for logical access; tenant scoping is an access-control decision.
Separate execution domains; covers 'cross-tenant execution impossible'.
Logical separation of information flows between tenants.
Cross-tenant leakage via shared resources.
Least privilege; here dynamic and task-scoped.
Associating security attributes with information; a taint mark is such an attribute.
Dynamically associate attributes as information is created and combined: the vocabulary for taint marking at ingestion and propagation.
Information flow enforcement between trust zones.
Dynamic information flow control: enforcement that changes with conditions, including detection of potentially harmful events.
Attribute-based access control is the mechanism class that could enforce it.
Name collision. SI-20 'Tainting' embeds markers to detect exfiltration of organisational data. IAM-10 taint-tracks inbound untrusted data to constrain privilege. Different concept.

qualifiers.subject: both
qualifiers.description: Do not treat these as equivalent on the strength of the shared word 'taint'. A reviewer mapping by title or keyword would wrongly report IAM-10 as covered by SI-20.

maps.remarks: Inventory of system components that accurately reflects the system; an unregistered tool is an inventory gap.
Deny-all, permit-by-exception for what may execute: the registry is the allowlist.
Detect unauthorized components and act on them: covers the unregistered-tool blind-spot clause.
Security approval before a tool enters service is configuration change control.
Enforce approved authorizations for access to the tool.
Only the tools the agent's function requires.
Uniquely identify and authenticate the calling service or application before communications.
Attribute-based policy is one way to bind agent to permitted tools.
Check validity of inputs: payload validation.
Monitor and control communications at managed interfaces: the gateway is the managed interface.
Enforce adherence to protocol formats: schema enforcement.
Rate limiting as denial-of-service protection.
Audit record generation for gateway events.
Validate output from programs to ensure it is consistent with expected content: structural validation of tool output.
From the agent's side, tool output is an information input to be checked for validity.
Prevent untrusted data injections: right intent, wrong mechanism for an LLM context. See qualifier.

qualifiers.subject: target
qualifiers.description: SI-10.6 is met by parameterized interfaces or output escaping, which separate data from code. A model reading tool output has no such separation: instructions and data share one channel. SI-10.6 can be satisfied literally (every conventional parser is protected) while tool-output injection into the model is unaddressed.

maps.remarks: Restrict inputs to trusted sources and approved formats; covers the structural half only.
Developer configuration management with integrity control over changes.
Cryptographic authentication of software components before installation.
Prevent installation of components without verification of a digital signature.
Enable integrity verification of software components.
Validate that a received component is genuine and not altered: the attestation clause.
Security validation gates in the pipeline are developer testing and evaluation.
Monitor and scan for vulnerabilities in the system and hosted applications; remediate.
Identify, report and correct flaws: the remediation half.
Automated vulnerability analysis in development, where the organisation is the developer.
Identify and address weaknesses in supply chain elements.
Malicious code protection is the nearest analogue for malicious model artifacts.
Risk assessment identifying threats and vulnerabilities; generic umbrella.
Threat modelling and vulnerability analyses during development; applies where the organisation develops the agent system.
Impact analysis before a change: adding a tool to the registry is such a change.
Separation of duties addresses conflicting capability combinations in people; the analogy to tools is loose.
Deny communications by default and allow by exception: the endpoint allow-list at the gateway.
Boundary protection at the managed interface.
Alert on defined indications of compromise: a non-tool API call is one.
Blocked calls are logged.
Configure the system to provide only essential capabilities.
Allow-by-exception for what may be invoked.
Secure defaults: nothing callable unless explicitly enabled.
Registry is the inventory (see TP-01).
Prohibit or restrict functions, ports, protocols and services.
Only allow incoming communications from defined sources: the inbound deny-by-default policy.
Deny by default, allow by exception.
Protect session authenticity, including against session hijacking: nearest home for origin-bound session handling.
Detect unauthorized local, network and remote connections.
Protect authenticators: covers the token-not-readable clause.
Restrict inputs to trusted sources: the untrusted-content classification, without the instruction-stripping.
Mobile code control and monitoring: covers scripts in pages, not hidden text instructions.
Detonation chambers for untrusted attachments: relevant to document-upload sanitisation.
Process isolation for the rendering component; does not address origin isolation.
Protect authenticity of sessions including against insertion of false information: forged session events.
Reference monitor: tamperproof, always invoked; the dispatch layer is this.
Irrefutable evidence an action was performed by an identified party; relevant to approval records.
Enforcement of authorizations at dispatch.
Integrity of the events and history the dispatcher trusts.
Policy governing software installation, with enforcement and monitoring.
Document, monitor and maintain valid provenance of components.
Operator allowlist of authorized software.
Validate a received component is genuine and not altered.
Signed-component verification, where the package ecosystem provides signatures.
Prevent installation without verification of a recognised digital signature.
Cryptographically authenticate components before installation.
Provenance end to end, publisher to artifact.
Skill privileges scoped to declared capability, not the agent's full identity.
Prevent download and execution of defined mobile code: relates to the runtime-fetch prohibition.
Component authenticity; framed around counterfeit, so only loosely applicable to malicious marketplace listings.
Separate execution domain per process: an in-process sandbox shares the host process, so arguably fails. See qualifier.

qualifiers.subject: both
qualifiers.description: To make SC-39 equivalent to TP-15, an assessor must interpret 'execution domain' as OS- or VM-enforced separation and reject in-process interpreter gates. SC-39 does not say so; an implementation using a hardened interpreter could be argued to pass SC-39 while failing TP-15.

maps.remarks: Execute in a confined physical or virtual environment with limited privileges.
Detonation chamber: isolated sandbox for executing untrusted code.
Boundary mechanisms isolating components; see EE-01.
Prevent untrusted data injections via parameterized interfaces: the launch path is a genuine data/code boundary, unlike TP-04.
Validate inputs: peer-supplied protocol metadata.
Restrict inputs to trusted sources and approved formats: origin-bound endpoints.
Deny-all, permit-by-exception for programs that may execute: allowlisted launch commands.
Prevent program execution per policy.
Managed information exchange with connected systems; onboarding and reconnection of tool servers.
Cryptographic protection of information at rest: weights at rest.
Key establishment and management; HSM-backed management is an organisation-defined requirement.
Cryptographic protection during transmission: weights in transit.
Determining and implementing the cryptography required for each use.
Integrity verification; nearest home for attestation of weights on edge devices.
Provenance of data and components: lineage for training datasets.
Integrity verification of information; catches tampering after approval, not poisoning before it. See qualifier.

qualifiers.subject: target
qualifiers.description: SI-7 can be satisfied in full while training data is poisoned: it detects unauthorised changes to information, and a poisoned sample inserted through a legitimate ingestion path is not one. Meeting MS-02 needs statistical validation in addition to SI-7.

maps.remarks: Access controls on training data.
Validate inputs at ingestion; covers the L2 format checks only.
Process to identify and address weaknesses in supply chain elements.
Document, monitor and maintain provenance of components and associated data.
Validate that a received component is genuine and not altered: pre-trained models from public hubs.
Assess and review suppliers, including public model repositories.
Cryptographic authentication of components before installation.
Signed components, where the model ecosystem provides signatures.
Organisation-wide supply chain risk management strategy.
Penetration testing: the periodic adversarial testing requirement. Also listed in NIST's predictive-AI overlay outline.
Input validation; covers structural checks, not instruction content.
Injection prevention; mechanism assumes parameterized interfaces. See qualifier and TP-04.

qualifiers.subject: target
qualifiers.description: SI-10.6 is met by parameterized interfaces or output escaping, which separate data from code. A model reads instructions and data in one channel, so SI-10.6 can be satisfied for every conventional parser while prompt injection is untouched.

maps.remarks: Restrict inputs to trusted sources and approved formats.
Policy filters on content, with hidden content named in guidance.
Red-team exercises: the L3/L4 red-teaming requirement.
Developer penetration testing: the pre-deployment adversarial test requirement. Also listed in NIST's predictive-AI overlay outline.
Output filtering: covers the L3 proxy-layer output guardrails only.
Validate output to ensure it is consistent with expected content.
Information flow control using content filters, with a defined response to filter failure.
Information flow enforcement between the model and its consumers.
Monitoring of outputs in production.
Inventory of system components that accurately reflects the system: 'what models do we have?'
Update the inventory on installation, removal and update: covers retirement.
Provenance and lineage of a component.
Baseline configuration under configuration control: versioning.
Inventory of organisational systems.
Developer configuration management.
Analyse changes in a separate test environment. See qualifier.

qualifiers.subject: both
qualifiers.description: CM-4.1 requires a separate test environment; MS-07 additionally requires that environment to be indistinguishable from production. Satisfying CM-4.1 with a clearly labelled, differently configured test environment is exactly what lets a model detect evaluation (see EE-04).

maps.remarks: Protect preproduction environments commensurate with risk.
Uniquely identify and authenticate services before communications: MCP gateway authentication.
Cryptographic authentication of components: signed tool metadata.
Validate responses against known-good schemas.
Authenticator management includes changing default authenticators before first use: the no-default-credentials clause.
Fail to a known state: authentication failure must not downgrade to anonymous.
Signed components.
Alert on defined indications of compromise: model-originated writes to execution-bearing locations.
Provenance for the trusted registry.
Content filters, with hidden content named in guidance.
Irrefutable evidence of what was approved; the approval record would need to include the rendered content.
Human reviews under defined conditions: the approval step whose fidelity MS-09 protects.
Authenticated, authorised writes to the memory store.
Cryptographic mechanisms to detect unauthorized changes to information: tamper-evident memory.
Audit record generation for memory writes.
Write-once media; loose analogue for append-only or immutable snapshots.
Anomaly detection on memory writes.
Eradication step of incident handling, applied to the memory store.
Restrict inputs to trusted sources: authenticated producers only.
Bind the identity of the information producer to the information.
Authenticate services before communications: ingestion pipelines authenticate producers.
Uniquely identify and authenticate source points for information transfer.
Monitoring; agent actions traced to a log entry would be flagged here.
Detect unauthorized changes to tool metadata against an approved baseline.
Cache entries served only within the authentication context that produced them.
Operator-approved baseline of tool metadata.
Prevent information transfer via shared resources: shared caches.
Cryptographic protection: signed cached metadata.
Restrict inputs to approved formats; covers length limits.
Cryptographic protection of the integrity of audit information.
Irrefutable evidence of what the model said.
Protect the authenticity of sessions, including insertion of false information.
Write-once media; loose analogue for an append-only transcript.
Cryptographic detection of unauthorized change.
Malicious code protection; worms are named, but as code.
Detect and deny outgoing traffic posing a threat to external systems.
Output filtering for content inconsistent with expected output.
Content filters on information flows.
Enforce authorizations at retrieval and write: ownership gating.
Logical separation of information flows between tenants.
Prevent unintended information transfer via shared resources: a pooled index.
Least common mechanism: design principle against shared mechanisms.
Minimized sharing.
Associate security and privacy attributes with information in storage, process and transmission.
Dynamically associate attributes as information is created and combined: classification at ingestion.
Security categorization of the information the system processes.
Flow decisions based on the attributes.
Protect confidentiality and integrity of transmitted information.
Cryptographic mechanisms during transmission.
Cryptography required for each use.
Key management.
Session authenticity.
Cryptographic protection of information at rest: encrypted memory.
Manage and retain information per requirements: retention policy.
Disposal of information after the retention period: automated purging.
Prevent information transfer via shared resources: cross-session leakage.
Media sanitization; literal media, loose analogue for purging memory.
Limit PII elements processed in the information life cycle.
Restrict processing of PII to what is authorized.
Least privilege, applied to data access.
Least privilege design principle.
Minimise PII used in testing, training and research.
Consent to processing of PII prior to collection.
Identify and restrict PII processing purposes.
Retention of information.
Minimise PII used in research, testing and training.
Provenance of data.
Data governance body.
Validate output to ensure consistency with expected content.
Content filters on information flows.
Monitor for evidence of unauthorized disclosure of information.
Prevent exfiltration.
Separation of duties: the agent cannot approve its own publication.
Developer configuration management with integrity control.
Cryptographic authentication before installation.
Access restrictions for change: writes to execution-bearing locations.
Dual authorization for defined actions.
Signed components.
Malware scanning of artifacts.
Deny by default, allow by exception: the destination allow-list.
Prevent exfiltration and test for it.
Covert channel analysis: finds channels not on the declared list.
Analyse outbound traffic for covert exfiltration.
Information flow enforcement to defined destinations.
Detect and deny outgoing traffic posing a threat.
Route traffic through authenticated proxies.
Identify the event types to be logged: every agent action.
Audit record content: type, time, location, source, outcome, identity.
Audit record generation.
Additional audit information: correlation to the initiating human session.
System-wide, time-correlated audit trail.
Session audit.
Develop profiles representing common traffic and event patterns and use them in monitoring.
Monitor to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks.
Analyse anomalous or suspected adversarial behaviour.
Analyse outbound traffic anomalies; covers unexpected listener and binding events.
Review and analyse audit records for unusual activity.
Capture the content of a session, in consultation with legal counsel.
Limit PII in audit records to elements identified in the privacy risk assessment: the sanitisation half. See qualifier.

qualifiers.subject: both
qualifiers.description: A prompt/response log is itself a new high-sensitivity data store. AU-3.3 ties the PII elements retained to a privacy risk assessment, so MIR-03 cannot be treated as met without one.

maps.remarks: Audit record content.
Additional audit information: prompt and response.
Protect audit information.
Retention for after-the-fact investigation.
Incident handling: preparation, detection, containment, eradication, recovery.
Incident response plan.

Automated incident handling: SOAR integration.
Automatic disabling of the system on defined conditions.
Incident response training.
Report incidents within a defined time to defined parties.

Breach handling, including notice to individuals and regulators.

Hardware-enforced write-once media.

Audit reduction and reporting supporting after-the-fact investigation.
Session audit.

Authorization to operate: approving agentic AI deployments.
Authorization process with designated roles.
Risk management strategy.
Data governance body; nearest named governance body, scoped to data.

Respond to findings in accordance with risk tolerance.
Plan of action and milestones: tracked to resolution.
Risk management strategy.
Automatic disabling of the system: closest to a kill switch.
Detect unauthorized components: unledgered-asset discovery.
Risk framing.
Rules of behaviour: the nearest policy-of-conduct control. See qualifier.

qualifiers.subject: target
qualifiers.description: PL-4 rules of behaviour are addressed to individuals with access to the system. An agent is not an individual, so applying PL-4 to agents is an interpretation. Autonomy tiers and transparency obligations are not part of PL-4.

maps.remarks: Limits on autonomy realised as least privilege.
Privacy notice; transparency obligation, scoped to PII.
Require external service providers to comply with security requirements; define oversight.
Assess and review suppliers.
Controls and processes for supply chain weaknesses.
Acquisition strategies and contract tools.
Security requirements in the acquisition contract.
Notification agreements and procedures.
Provide incident information to supply chain organisations.
Supply chain risk assessment.
Continuous monitoring with defined metrics and reporting.
Organisation-wide continuous monitoring strategy.
Control assessments and reporting of results.
Measures of performance, monitored and reported.
